Native check: Hrvatski

Native speaker? Each line below is from the book. Read it and its question, then tap Correct if it is fine as it is, or Needs change and write what you would say instead. Answer as many lines as you like.

Line 1

S ove strane odmotavam nit riječi, a s druge strane ti skupljaš riječi.

The author unravels a thread of words; the reader gathers them. Does this read naturally?

Line 2

Idi i van. Idi na mirna mjesta.

Maman mispronounces quiet on purpose. Does 'mirna' work as her mispronunciation?

Line 3

– Viiiž, Baba, Baba, hoćeš li mi kupiti ovu veliku lutku?

A toddler asks her dad for a doll. Does it sound like baby talk?

Line 4

Čovjeka uhvati govnovrtoglavica. Što više razmišljaš o tome, sve te jače hvata govnovrtoglavica.

A student's crude made-up word for dizziness. Is 'govnovrtoglavica' understandable?

Line 5

Srce mi je vedro pri pomisli da ćemo jednog dana sjediti jedno nasuprot drugome u kafiću, za stolom, kraj prozora, i dok kiša nježno sjeda na staklo, čitat ću joj priču, a ona će slušati sa zadovoljnim osmijehom.

Amir imagines reading his story to Niloofar in a cafe. Does this read naturally?

Line 6

– I ti, s tim svojim kurčevitim načinom govora, trebao si se zvati Alat Delon.

The nickname is meant as a rude pun on Alain Delon. Does it work?

Line 7

Za norouz stolom, kad sam čitao pjesmu za majku, Maman je umjesto da se raduje postala uznemirena.

He read the poem at the exact moment the year turned. Is that clear?

Line 8

Maman je bacila moj madrac na vrh dvorišnog zida.

Maman simply put his mattress up on the wall, without anger. Is that clear?

Line 9

– Zove se Quchan Bazaar i naša kuća je na kraju Quchan Bazaara.

Does 'Quchan Bazaar' sound natural as the name of the market?

Line 10

– To je mramal. Mramal znači jako skupo.

A child mispronounces marble and thinks the word means expensive. Is that clear?

Line 11

– Ali, eto, zeznuo je. Orlovo Oko kaže per tu per, a Taverni kaže Stari tu Stari.

Taverny (Amir) misheard peer as pir, Persian for elder. Does the joke work?

Line 12

– Da, kupit ću ti lutku. Kad mi dođe novac, kupit ću ti i bolju od te, Babina djevojčice.

The dad playfully echoes his toddler's baby talk. Does that come through?

Line 13

"Ono vino što je onde istina je, ne metafora."

This Hafez line should allow two readings: real wine, and only a metaphor. Does it?

Line 14

Uvjeren da će mi odgovoriti, nazvah Maman i rekoh da su nam organizirali dopunsku nastavu pa moram ostati duže.

His made-up excuse is extra classes. Does 'dopunsku nastavu' mean that?

Line 15

Zemlju su nasipali burdožerom. Zemlju i vapno.

Maman mispronounces bulldozer on purpose. Is that clear?

Line 16

Khe, khe. Vukao si nas amo-tamo.

Does 'Vukao si nas amo-tamo' mean you wore us out?
